fit: visual symptom prevalence in tau PET diagnostic syndromes
assessment: Clinical presence was reported for 13 of 33 with dementia with Lewy bodies and two of 18 with posterior cortical atrophy. The study compares clinical syndromes and tracer uptake without a culinary exposure or timed visual episode rate.

fit: clinician concerns about levodopa and visual hallucinations
assessment: The survey compares 100 neurologists with 100 psychiatrists. Possible visual symptom worsening influenced reported prescribing decisions for dementia with Lewy bodies. The questionnaire does not count clinical visual episodes after assigned food or medication.

fit: follow-up diagnosis and visual symptom presence in an FDG-PET cohort
assessment: Seventy-two patients ultimately met dementia-with-Lewy-bodies criteria. Visual symptom presence was part of clinical ascertainment, with family observations and uncertainty in some entry records. It provides no dried fig timing or episode count.

fit: pimavanserin and chart-recorded global psychosis improvement
assessment: Clinical improvement was documented for 69 of 91 treated patients in an uncontrolled retrospective review. The outcome spans forms of Parkinson-related psychosis. It does not estimate a separate visual episode rate or food effect.

fit: functional imaging dynamics and visual symptom severity
assessment: The original reports no clear association of selected dynamic imaging measures with visual hallucination severity in the clinical dementia-with-Lewy-bodies group. This concerns imaging correlation and does not address dried fig intake.

fit: patient and caregiver recognition of a visual symptom
assessment: The visual item was recognized by 40.6% of 32 patients and 39.3% of 28 caregivers. These are responses on Parkinson disease knowledge, with no assessment of food exposure or observed episodes.

fit: new postoperative visual hallucination in a Parkinson stimulation cohort
assessment: The 36-person pre-post surgical study lists one person with a new visual hallucination after subthalamic stimulation. Symptom onset for one patient does not establish a repeated visual episode frequency or a dried fig exposure effect.

fit: specific hallucination subscale in a registered Lewy body stimulation crossover
assessment: The six-person crossover was reported first in the 2019 congress. Table 2 covers five analyzable NPI records. The median hallucination subscale difference is zero for active versus sham, p = 0.655, while the total score contrast is -13, p = 0.066. The prespecified visual interview is distinct. No fig exposure is present.

fit: medication crossover and robot-induced sensed presence in Parkinson disease
assessment: Twenty people completed the analyzed crossover. A stronger induced presence response during prescribed dopaminergic treatment was reported in the 11 with prior spontaneous hallucinations. This is an experimentally provoked phenomenon, distinct from spontaneous visual episode frequency following food. Participant overlap with the July preprint remains unverified.
